payload.reason: The evidence indicates that the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) melts before the Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) due to specific climatic and geological conditions during the Last Interglacial (LIG), leading to distinct sea level changes.

claims.text: The Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) begins to melt before the Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS), contributing to an early peak in sea level during the Last Interglacial (LIG).
The melting of GrIS contributes 2 m to sea level rise at 125 ka, while AIS starts melting later, contributing 5 m at 118 ka, indicating a sequential melting pattern.
The timing of GrIS and AIS melting produces substantial visible changes in the stratigraphic record, supporting the idea of distinct melting phases.
